Paper Title: A Hybrid Neural Network Model for Sentiment Analysis of Financial Texts Using Topic Extraction, Pre-Trained Model, and Enhanced Attention Mechanism Methods (Duan et al., 2024)
Dataset: FiQA Task1 & SemEval 2017 Task 5 (training); FinancialPhraseBank, StockSen, SEntFiN (evaluation)
Theme: Hybrid neural networks for financial sentiment analysis
Methodology Adopted: LFBP framework: LDA-based topic layer + FinBERT + BiGRU + Progressive Attention (adaptive threshold + weight masking)
Accuracy: F1-score improvement of 2.05%–7.27% over all baselines
Detailed Description: Proposes LFBP model that fuses topic features to resolve context collapse, FinBERT for domain language, BiGRU for sequential features, and improved attention to reduce single-word noise, delivering more stable sentiment classification on financial texts.
Shortcomings/gaps: Traditional LDA yields lower topic coherence (~0.4–0.5) than VAE methods; attention not specialised for numerical magnitude → scalar blindness remains; purely static analysis, no year-over-year risk trajectory.
Scope for Improvements: A Hybrid Neural Network Model for Sentiment Analysis of Financial Texts Using Topic Extraction, Pre-Trained Model, and Enhanced Attention Mechanism Methods (Duan et al., 2024)

Paper Title: Joint Topic-Emotion Modeling in Financial Texts: A Novel Approach to Investor Sentiment and Market Trends (Mir et al., 2025)
Dataset: Global financial news + social media corpus; StockEmotions dataset for emotion labels
Theme: Joint topic-emotion modeling in financial discourse
Methodology Adopted: Neural Variational Document Model (NVDM) for latent topics + fine-tuned FinBERT for emotion classification
Accuracy:
Topic: coherence 0.68, perplexity –8.5
Emotion: accuracy 96.3%, F1 97.8%, precision 98.3%, recall 97.5%
Detailed Description: Uses NVDM (VAE-based) to discover coherent financial topics and FinBERT to associate them with fine-grained investor emotions, providing richer market-trend insights than isolated topic or sentiment models.
Shortcomings/gaps: Static joint modelling only; no temporal evolution across reporting periods; no explicit numerical-magnitude handling; lacks external-news grounding for auditability.
Scope for Improvements: Extend with BiGRU-Attention for semantic drift detection between consecutive annual reports; integrate TNCRM masking for scalar awareness; add RAG dashboard for quantitative risk scoring and paragraph-level explanations → FinRisk-Evo’s Evolution + Precision engines.

Paper Title: Enhancing Financial Sentiment Analysis Ability of Language Model via Targeted Numerical Change-Related Masking (Jung & Jang, 2024)
Theme: Post-training to overcome scalar blindness in financial PLMs
Methodology Adopted: Targeted Numerical Change-Related Masking (TNCRM): 193-word increase/decrease list preferentially masked during post-training of FinBERT (and other PLMs) on 50k financial news sentences
Accuracy: Optimal at 50,000 sentences; substantial gains in accuracy & weighted F1 (especially in low-resource 10–20% train splits) vs. vanilla FinBERT
Detailed Description: Creates a masking list of 193 numerical-change words, forces the model to predict them during post-training, dramatically improving magnitude awareness (e.g., correctly classifying “loss reduced from €2.2M to €0.3M” as positive).
Shortcomings/gaps: Only addresses numerical sensitivity; no topic modelling for context collapse; no temporal logic across fiscal years; evaluated only on news sentences, not full annual reports.
Scope for Improvements: Combine TNCRM with NVDM topic isolation, BiGRU-Attention for year-to-year vector drift, and RAG for external-news validation on real annual reports → FinRisk-Evo’s complete “Precision + Context + Evolution” hybrid pipeline.

Paper Title: A Hybrid LSTM-GRU Model for Stock Price Prediction (Farhadi et al., 2025)
Dataset: Tehran Stock Exchange (TSE) data; specific stocks not named in abstract; size not specified (historical prices)
Theme: Hybrid recurrent networks for stock price forecasting
Methodology Adopted: Hybrid LSTM-GRU model; machine learning for feature extraction (technical indicators); weight matrix adjustment; LSTM for long dependencies, GRU for short
Accuracy: MSE improvement of 3% over baselines (e.g., LSTM, GRU alone)
Detailed Description: Combines LSTM and GRU to capture long and short-term dependencies in stock sequences, using ML to select and weight technical features; evaluated on TSE market for chaotic fluctuations.
Shortcomings/gaps: Difficulty in hyperparameter tuning; limited to TSE market; no sentiment or numerical magnitude focus; lacks temporal risk drift detection.
Scope for Improvements: Integrate TNCRM for numerical sensitivity; add NVDM for thematic context; enhance with BiGRU-Attention for FY drift and RAG for validation → align with FinRisk-Evo's hybrid for risk intelligence.

Paper Title: Smart Analysis of Economics Sentiment in Spanish Based on Linguistic Features and Transformers (García-Díaz et al., 2023)
Dataset: Custom corpus of 15,915 tweets annotated as positive, negative, or neutral; source: Compiled from Spanish financial texts
Theme: Sentiment analysis in Spanish financial texts
Methodology Adopted: Feature sets: Contextual/non-contextual embeddings (e.g., transformers) + linguistic features; knowledge integration for combination; classifiers not specified in abstract
Detailed Description: Explores combination of embeddings and linguistic features for SA in Spanish financial texts; achieves best results with integrated feature sets for polarity classification.
Shortcomings/gaps: Challenges in low-resource languages like Spanish; context-dependent terms and polysemy not fully handled; no temporal or numerical magnitude focus.
Scope for Improvements: Add TNCRM masking for numerical triggers; incorporate NVDM for topic isolation; use BiGRU for temporal evolution; RAG for auditability → enhance FinRisk-Evo's applicability to multilingual financial reports.

Paper Title: PyFin-sentiment: Towards a machine-learning-based model for deriving sentiment from financial tweets (Wilksch & Abramova, 2023)
Dataset: Custom dataset of 10,000 finance/investing tweets, manually labeled with market sentiment
Theme: Domain-specific sentiment analysis for financial tweets
Methodology Adopted: Benchmarking VADER, NTUSD-Fin, FinBERT, TwitterRoBERTa; new logistic regression model trained on labeled data; deployed as Python library
Accuracy: Outperforms baselines on Twitter (specific F1/precision/recall not detailed); on par with BERT on other platforms
Detailed Description: Collects and labels 10,000 tweets for market sentiment; trains simple logistic regression that outperforms generics due to domain vocabulary; lower cost than deep models.
Shortcomings/gaps: Existing models fail on specialized financial vocabulary; limited to tweets, not reports; no temporal or numerical focus.
Scope for Improvements: Combine with TNCRM for magnitude awareness; NVDM for topics; BiGRU-Attention for drift; RAG dashboard → extend FinRisk-Evo to social media risk tracking.

Paper Title: Recent advancements and challenges of NLP-based sentiment analysis: A state-of-the-art review (Jim et al., 2024)
Dataset: Various datasets reviewed (e.g., in healthcare, finance); no specific new dataset; sources like Twitter, reviews
Theme: Survey of SA advancements and challenges
Methodology Adopted: Reviews ML, DL, LLMs, pre-trained models (e.g., BERT, FinBERT) for SA; multimodal approaches
Accuracy: Various accuracies from reviewed works (e.g., F1 up to 97% in some DL models); no single metric
Detailed Description: Comprehensive review of SA applications, techniques, datasets, metrics; discusses ML/DL/LLM pros/cons, challenges like sarcasm.
Shortcomings/gaps: Gaps in multimodal SA, label perspectives; biases in datasets; lack of temporal dynamics in many models.
Scope for Improvements: Incorporate temporal modules like BiGRU; TNCRM for scalars; NVDM + RAG for context/auditability → inspire FinRisk-Evo's hybrid for financial gaps.

Paper Title: Predicting stock price trends using language models to extract the sentiment from analyst reports: Evidence from IBEX 35-listed companies (Moreno et al., 2025)
Dataset: 379 analyst reports for 10 IBEX 35 companies (2016-2022); source: Bloomberg; 303 train, 76 test
Theme: LLM sentiment extraction from analyst reports for stock trends
Methodology Adopted: Fine-tuned RoBERTa, FinBERT, GPT for sentiment; bag-of-words; price movement over horizons
Accuracy: Weighted F1 0.76-1.00 for consistency; precision 0.29-0.53 for prediction
Detailed Description: Uses LLMs to extract unbiased sentiment from reports; predicts trends, outperforms analysts in precision; highlights biases.
Shortcomings/gaps: Low precision (<50%); limited reports post-MiFID II; no fine-tuning for GPT; event noise.
Scope for Improvements: Add TNCRM for magnitudes; NVDM topics; BiGRU drift; RAG validation → integrate into FinRisk-Evo for annual report analysis.

Paper Title: A Dual Output Temporal Convolutional Network With Attention Architecture for Stock Price Prediction and Risk Assessment (Biswas et al., 2025)
Dataset: MasterCard (MA) and Visa (V) data (2008-2024); size: 15+ years daily
Theme: Dual-output DL for price prediction and risk assessment
Methodology Adopted: TCN with attention; dual output for prices (Open/Close/High/Low) and risk (volatility, Sharpe); dilated convolutions
Accuracy: MAE 1.23 (MA), 1.45 (V); volatility MAE 0.012, Sharpe 0.065; backtest MAE 1.25/1.50
Detailed Description: Integrates TCN-attention for temporal dependencies; predicts prices and risks simultaneously; outperforms LSTM/ARIMA.
Shortcomings/gaps: Nonlinear/noisy data; limited to MA/V; no sentiment or topic integration.
Scope for Improvements: Add TNCRM numerical; NVDM topics; BiGRU drift; RAG dashboard → boost FinRisk-Evo's evolution engine for risk dashboards.

Detailed Description: Fuses prices, indicators, news sentiment; outperforms baselines in accuracy/portfolio returns.
